manual.text: We used to build the world's railways because we just got on with it. The talent is still here in our towns, we’ve just let the clipboard brigade convince us we've lost our touch.

evening.text: Walked past the old steelworks tonight. We used to build the world, now we need a risk assessment to open a window. The genius is still here, we just need to trust our own backbone again.
We didn't become a brilliant country by filling in risk assessments. The ingenuity is still here, waiting in sheds and workshops. Our best days aren't in history books, they're next.

morning.text: Kettle's on. Sick of being told our best days are behind us by people who couldn't wire a plug. We've got the brains and the heritage, we just need to stop apologising and get on with it.

evening.text: We spent centuries inventing the future in drafty sheds. The talent is still here, we've just got more paperwork. Shift the red tape and we'll surprise them all again.

morning.text: We used to build railways across continents, now we get stage fright over a simple bypass. The talent and grit are still in our workshops. We just need to take the handbrake off.

evening.text: We used to build railways that changed the world on a handshake. The ingenuity is still in our towns, we just need to start trusting our own hands again instead of the clipboard brigade.
